result.summary: Disconnect peers that send a SENDTXRCNCL message after VERACK even when local transaction reconciliation is disabled. The check for post-VERACK receipt is moved ahead of the early return for nodes running without txreconciliation enabled.
result.problem: When -txreconciliation is disabled (the default), nodes ignore SENDTXRCNCL messages received after VERACK instead of disconnecting the peer as mandated by BIP 330.
evidence: "As mandated by BIP 330... always disconnect such a peer, regardless of the value of -txreconciliation." (PR description)
result.changed_since_previous: No functional change; the patch is now available and confirms the reordering of the checks in ProcessMessage.
result.card: Enforces BIP 330 compliance by unconditionally disconnecting peers that send a SENDTXRCNCL message after VERACK. Previously, nodes running without transaction reconciliation enabled (-txreconciliation=0) ignored the message instead of disconnecting the misbehaving peer. The change reorders the check in net_processing to evaluate connection state before checking local feature enablement.

risk.why: A mistake in P2P message validation logic could result in spuriously disconnecting legitimate peers.
